History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
23-year-old male with 1-week history of sore throat progressing to dry cough and mild exertional shortness of breath; clinically consistent with self-limiting upper respiratory tract infection. Reassurance, symptomatic care, sick note, and safety-net advice provided.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sore throat × 1 week followed by dry cough.  
• Timeline:
  – Day 0 (Thu/Fri last week): Sore throat began.  
  – Day 1–2: Dry cough developed.  
  – Day 4–5: Onset of mild shortness of breath; persists.  
• Symptom character & modifiers:
  – Cough: Dry, non-productive, no diurnal variation, no hemoptysis.  
  – Shortness of breath: Only on exertion (able to manage stairs/exercise), not at rest.  
  – Wheeze and mild chest discomfort reported.  
  – Feverish feelings during first 3 days, now resolved.  
  – Intermittent headaches.  
  – Appetite reduced; denies weight loss.  
  – No nasal or sinus congestion; no rash.  
• Review of systems: No night sweats, no leg swelling, no calf pain, no pleuritic chest pain reported.  
• Patient concerns: Ruled-out serious causes (TB, cancer); requests reassurance, treatment advice, and sick note.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions.  
• No asthma; no venous thromboembolism history.

Social History:
• Born in USA; resident in UK for past 12 years.  
• Travel: Only routine trips within Europe; none recently to high-risk areas.  
• Smoking: Non-smoker (experimented “once or twice” only).  
• Alcohol/substance use: Not discussed.  
• Occupational/financial: Requires sick note for work absence.  
• Asbestos exposure: None known.

Family History:
• Mother – lung cancer.  
• No other significant familial diseases reported.

Physical Examination:
(No in-person exam performed; video assessment only)  
• Patient reports no palpable neck lumps; throat not visualised.  
• Vitals: Not obtained.

Investigations:
• None performed or available.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Upper respiratory tract infection / viral pharyngitis with reactive dry cough
  – Likely viral etiology given timeline, self-limited fever, lack of sputum.  
  – Advice: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) for analgesia/pyrexia, maintain adequate oral hydration, rest, and monitor symptoms.  
  – Expect improvement over next 4–5 days.  
  – Safety-net: Seek in-person GP review or emergency care if breathlessness acutely worsens, develops resting dyspnea, produces blood-stained sputum, persistent fever, or if no improvement after 5 days.

Issue 2: Patient work absence
  – Issued digital sick note for additional days off work as requested.

Issue 3: Cancer/TB health anxiety
  – Provided reassurance: Current presentation not suggestive of tuberculosis or lung cancer; low risk due to age, non-smoker status, symptom pattern.  
  – Reinforced need for follow-up if symptoms persist or new red-flag features arise.

General plan items:
• No prescriptions other than OTC paracetamol recommended.  
• No immediate investigations indicated; re-evaluate if symptoms persist/worsen.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing elements: No vitals, physical exam limited; complete medication list, alcohol intake not elicited.  
• Internal conflicts: Patient initially denied then confirmed shortness of breath (conflict noted).  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational overlaps, otherwise intelligible.
